To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the study species are exploited for different purposes and are in varying conservation status.

The study revealed that the species are multipurpose, exploited to satisfy different human needs and have a good conservation status, except for the species Securidaca Longipedunculata which was not encountered in the study plots, and the species Acacia seyal and Acacia hocki which had a moderate status.
the study revealed that 16 species were used for various purposes, and that the majority of them are threatened.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sustainable management of woody resources in Gadumire.
the conservation of woody species in the face of human pressure.
documenting local knowledge and the ecology of selected woody species in Gadumire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 16 woody plants of Gadumire have an overall good conservation status.
all the species in this study are threatened with extinction and need to be conserved in the study area and in the whole of Uganda.
the species are threatened and that the threats need to be managed to ensure the sustainable use of these resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the species Acacia hoffii, Albizia coriari, Markhamia Lutea and Albizizygia are in good conservation status.
the species have been overexploited and that the community needs to be educated and empowered to conserve and manage the species for sustainable utilization.
the species are threatened and that the community is aware of the threats and has some solutions to the problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local knowledge is a valuable tool in the conservation of natural resources.
there is a need to integrate community perceptions and ecological data to guide the management of natural resources.
there is a need for the conservation of the woody resources in Gadumire, and this can best be achieved by the community through the adoption of sustainable use practices.
